title: Number Systems
description: Learn the different types of numbers, their properties, relationships, and how to classify and compare them.

content.title: What Are Numbers?
content.content: Numbers are symbols used to represent quantities, values, measurements, and positions. In mathematics, numbers allow us to describe quantities and perform operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

content.title: Using Numbers
content.question: What number represents the quantity of 8 apples?
content.solution: The number 8 represents the quantity because there are eight apples.

content.question: What is one common purpose of numbers?
content.explanation: Numbers are used to represent quantities, values, measurements, positions, and many other mathematical ideas.

content.title: Natural Numbers
content.content: Natural numbers are the positive counting numbers. In this course, natural numbers begin with 1 and continue indefinitely: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so on.

content.title: Identifying Natural Numbers
content.question: Which of the following are natural numbers: 2, 5, 9, and 12?
content.solution: All four numbers are positive counting numbers. Therefore, they are natural numbers.

content.question: Which of the following is a natural number?
content.explanation: Under the definition used in this course, natural numbers begin with 1 and include positive counting numbers such as 7.

content.title: Whole Numbers
content.content: Whole numbers include all natural numbers together with zero. They are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on. Unlike natural numbers in this course, whole numbers include 0.

content.title: Natural Numbers vs Whole Numbers
content.question: Is 0 a natural number or a whole number?
content.solution: In this course, natural numbers begin with 1, while whole numbers include 0. Therefore, 0 is a whole number but not a natural number.

content.question: Which number is a whole number but not a natural number?
content.explanation: Whole numbers include 0, while natural numbers in this course begin with 1.

content.title: Integers
content.content: Integers are numbers that include positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero. They continue indefinitely in both directions: ..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...

content.title: Identifying Integers
content.question: Which of the following are integers: -6, 2.5, 0, and 9?
content.solution: Integers do not contain decimal or fractional parts. Therefore, -6, 0, and 9 are integers, while 2.5 is not.

content.question: Which number is NOT an integer?
content.explanation: Integers are positive and negative whole numbers together with zero. 4.5 has a decimal part, so it is not an integer.

content.title: Rational Numbers
content.content: A rational number is any number that can be written as a fraction a/b, where a and b are integers and b is not zero. Rational numbers include integers, fractions, terminating decimals, and repeating decimals.
content.formula: a/b, where a, b ∈ ℤ and b ≠ 0

content.title: Identifying Rational Numbers
content.question: Is 0.75 a rational number?
content.solution: Yes. 0.75 can be written as 75/100, which simplifies to 3/4. Since 3 and 4 are integers and the denominator is not zero, 0.75 is rational.

content.question: Which number is rational?
content.explanation: 3/5 is a ratio of two integers with a nonzero denominator, so it is a rational number.

content.title: Irrational Numbers
content.content: Irrational numbers are numbers that cannot be written as a ratio of two integers. Their decimal representations are non-terminating and non-repeating. Common examples include π, √2, and √3.

content.title: Identifying Irrational Numbers
content.question: Is √2 rational or irrational?
content.solution: √2 cannot be expressed as a fraction of two integers. Its decimal representation continues indefinitely without repeating a fixed pattern. Therefore, √2 is irrational.

content.question: Which number is irrational?
content.explanation: √2 cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers, so it is irrational.

content.title: Real Numbers
content.content: Real numbers include all rational and irrational numbers. Every real number can be represented as a point on the real number line. Examples include integers, fractions, decimals, square roots of positive numbers, and π.

content.title: Identifying Real Numbers
content.question: Is √2 a real number?
content.solution: Yes. √2 is an irrational number, and all irrational numbers are part of the real number system.

content.question: Which number is NOT a real number?
content.explanation: √-1 is not a real number. It is associated with the imaginary unit i.

content.title: Classifying Numbers
content.content: A number can belong to more than one number set. For example, 5 is a natural number, whole number, integer, rational number, and real number. Classification means identifying all the number sets to which a number belongs.

content.title: Classifying 5
content.question: Which number sets contain 5?
content.solution: 5 is a natural number. Every natural number is also a whole number and an integer. Every integer is rational, and every rational number is real.

content.question: Which number belongs to the natural, whole, integer, rational, and real number sets?
content.explanation: 5 is a natural number, so it is also a whole number, integer, rational number, and real number.

content.title: Number Sets and Relationships
content.content: The common number sets are related through inclusion. Natural numbers are contained within the whole numbers, whole numbers are contained within the integers, and integers are contained within the rational numbers. Rational and irrational numbers together make up the real numbers.

content.title: Classifying -3
content.question: Classify the number -3.
content.solution: -3 is an integer. Since every integer can be written as a fraction with denominator 1, -3 is also rational. Every rational number is real.

content.question: Which statement about number sets is correct?

options.text: Every integer is a natural number.
Every whole number is an integer.
Every real number is an integer.

content.explanation: Whole numbers such as 0, 1, 2, and 3 are all integers. However, negative integers are not whole numbers.

content.title: Comparing Real Numbers
content.content: Real numbers can be compared using greater than (>), less than (<), and equal to (=). On a number line, a number farther to the right is greater than a number farther to the left.

content.title: Comparing Negative Numbers
content.question: Which is greater: -2 or -5?
content.solution: On the number line, -2 is located to the right of -5. Therefore, -2 is greater than -5.

content.question: Which statement is true?
content.explanation: -3 is farther to the right on the number line than -7, so -3 is greater than -7.

content.title: Ordering Real Numbers
content.content: Real numbers can be arranged from least to greatest or from greatest to least. When ordering numbers on a number line, numbers farther to the left are smaller and numbers farther to the right are greater.

content.title: Ordering Numbers
content.question: Order the numbers -3, 1, -1, and 4 from least to greatest.
content.solution: Place the numbers on a number line. The numbers from left to right are -3, -1, 1, and 4.

content.question: Which list shows the numbers in order from least to greatest?
content.explanation: Numbers increase from left to right on the number line. Therefore, the correct order is -4, -1, 1, 3.

content.title: Absolute Value
content.content: The absolute value of a number represents its distance from zero on the number line. Distance is always non-negative, so the absolute value of any real number is greater than or equal to zero.

content.title: Finding Absolute Value
content.question: Find the absolute value of -8.
content.solution: -8 is 8 units away from zero on the number line. Therefore, its absolute value is 8.

content.question: What is the value of |-12|?
content.explanation: Absolute value represents distance from zero. Since -12 is 12 units from zero, |-12| = 12.

content.title: The Number Line
content.content: A number line represents numbers as points along a line. Zero is the reference point. Positive numbers are located to the right of zero, while negative numbers are located to the left. Numbers increase as you move to the right and decrease as you move to the left.

content.title: Using the Number Line
content.question: Which number is farther to the left on the number line: -4 or 2?
content.solution: -4 is located to the left of 2 on the number line because -4 is less than 2.

content.question: Which number is located farthest to the right?
content.explanation: Numbers increase from left to right on the number line. Therefore, 4 is farthest to the right.
